title: Successive local quotients of a relative global complete intersection are flat over the base
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P$. Suppose $S=P/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$, let $\mathfrak q'$ be its inverse image in $P$; for each $0\le i\le c$, the ring $P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f_1,\dots,f_i)P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal), part (2), algebra.tex lines 36767-36820

proof.text: Notation: $\mathfrak p\subset R$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$ under $R\to S$; since $R\to S$ factors as $R\to P\to S$, $\mathfrak p$ is also the inverse image of $\mathfrak q'$ under $R\to P$. Since $f_1,\dots,f_c$ map to $0\in\mathfrak q$, all $f_j\in\mathfrak q'$. For $0\le i\le c$ put $M_i=P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f_1,\dots,f_i)P_{\mathfrak q'}$, an $R$-module via $R\to P\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$. Claim (N): the statement holds when $R$ is in addition Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Steps 1-3 prove (N); in them $R$ is Noetherian. By the definition of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] the monomials $x^\alpha$ form a basis of $P$ as an $R$-module, so $P$ is a free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and hence flat [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]; $P$ is a finite type $R$-algebra, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] applied to the flat map $R\to P$ and the prime $\mathfrak q'$ (with inverse image $\mathfrak p$), the induced map $\phi:R_{\mathfrak p}\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$, $r/s\mapsto r/s$, is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. The maximal ideal of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and the ideal of $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ generated by $\phi(\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p})$ is $\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$, the ideal generated by the $a/1$, $a\in\mathfrak p$ (as $\phi(a/s)=(a/1)(s/1)^{-1}$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), first paragraph: 'the local ring R[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'} is flat over R_p' and 'R, and hence R[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'} is Noetherian'; Lemma Tag 00HT (6), Lemma Tag 00FN

proof.text: (Still $R$ Noetherian.) The images of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ in $P_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$ form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Let $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $C=P\otimes_Rk$ and $j:P\to C$, $h\mapsto h\otimes1$; for $h\in P$ let $\bar h\in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be $h$ with its coefficients mapped by $R\to k$. (a) [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] (with $A=R$, coefficient ring $k$, variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$) gives an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $k\otimes_RP\to k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $\lambda\otimes h\mapsto\lambda\bar h$; composed with the swap $C=P\otimes_Rk\cong k\otimes_RP$ it is a ring isomorphism $\sigma:C\to k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with $\sigma(j(h))=\bar h$. (b) Since $\mathfrak q'$ is a prime of $P$ over $\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] (with $A=R$, $B=P$) gives a prime $\mathfrak Q\subset C$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q'$. Put $\mathfrak q''=\sigma(\mathfrak Q)$, a prime of $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$; as $f_j\in\mathfrak q'$, $\bar f_j=\sigma(j(f_j))\in\mathfrak q''$. (c) Let $J=(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $T=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/J$. By part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change] for $R\to k$, $T$ is a relative global complete intersection over $k$. The only prime of the field $k$ is $(0)$, and $\kappa((0))=k_{(0)}=k$ (nonzero elements are already units), so the fibre ring of $T$ over $(0)$ is $T\otimes_kk\cong T$; it is nonzero because $J\subseteq\mathfrak q''\neq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], $\operatorname{Spec}T$ has Krull dimension $n-c$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-local-regular-sequence] (field $k$, $m=n$, $t=c$, the $\bar f_j$, the prime $\mathfrak q''\supseteq J$) shows that $\bar f_1/1,\dots,\bar f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\mathfrak q''}$. (d) As $\sigma$ maps $\mathfrak Q$ onto $\mathfrak q''$ and $C\setminus\mathfrak Q$ onto the complement of $\mathfrak q''$, it induces a ring isomorphism $C_{\mathfrak Q}\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\mathfrak q''}$, $j(h)/1\mapsto\bar h/1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-natural-iso] (with $A=R$, $B=P$, the prime $\mathfrak Q$, so $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q'$) the map $h/s\mapsto j(h)/j(s)$ induces a ring isomorphism $P_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}\cong C_{\mathfrak Q}$. The composite ring isomorphism $P_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\mathfrak q''}$ sends the class of $f_j/1$ to $\bar f_j/1$; a ring isomorphism carries the ideal generated by elements to the ideal generated by their images, hence quotients to quotients and injective multiplications to injective multiplications, so by the definition [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] the classes of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ form a regular sequence in $P_{\mathfrak q'}/\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), first paragraph: 'By Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci) for example we see that f_1,...,f_c form a regular sequence in the local ring R[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'} (x)_R kappa(p)', via the last paragraph of the proof of Lemma Tag 00SC (line 35909); Remark Tag 0H9M (line 3520); Lemma Tag 00SS (1) for the fibre

proof.text: (Still $R$ Noetherian; end of the proof of (N).) By [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-regular-sequence-flat] applied to the flat local homomorphism $\phi:R_{\mathfrak p}\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$ of Noetherian local rings (Step 1, where the ideal generated by the image of the maximal ideal is $\mathfrak pP_{\mathfrak q'}$) and to $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ (Step 2), each $M_i=P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f_1,\dots,f_i)P_{\mathfrak q'}$, $0\le i\le c$, is a flat $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module (via $\phi$). The $R$-module structure of $M_i$ is the restriction of this one along $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, as both come from $R\to P\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] (with $A=R$, $W=R\setminus\mathfrak p$, $A'=R_{\mathfrak p}$) $M_i$ is a flat $R$-module. This proves (N).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), first paragraph: 'we see from Lemma 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence) that (1) and (2) hold'; flatness over R from flatness over R_p by Lemma Tag 00HT (2)

proof.text: General $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-noetherian-approximation] there is a subring $R_0\subseteq R$, generated as a ring by finitely many elements, containing all coefficients of the $f_j$, with $R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ a relative global complete intersection over $R_0$. Let $\Lambda$ be the set of subrings $R_\lambda\subseteq R$ which contain $R_0$ and are generated as rings by finitely many elements (finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]), ordered by inclusion. $R_0\in\Lambda$; two members $R_\lambda,R_\mu$ lie in the subring generated by the union of finite generating sets of both, which is in $\Lambda$; and every $r\in R$ lies in the subring generated by $r$ and generators of $R_0$; so $\Lambda$ is directed with union $R$. Each $R_\lambda$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] over the Noetherian ring $\mathbf Z$ (every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). The $f_j$ lie in $R_0[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the inclusion $R_0\to R_\lambda$ maps them to themselves, so part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-base-change] shows that $S_\lambda=R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $R_\lambda$. For $\lambda\le\mu$ we have subrings $R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq R_\mu[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subseteq P$ (polynomials with coefficients in $R_\lambda$, resp. $R_\mu$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), second paragraph: R written as the filtered colimit of its finite type Z-subalgebras containing R_0 of Lemma Tag 00SU (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-Noetherian), S_lambda a relative global complete intersection by Lemma Tag 00SS (lemma-base-change-relative-global-complete-intersection)

proof.text: Fix $0\le i\le c$. For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $\mathfrak q'_\lambda=\mathfrak q'\cap R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, a prime ideal of $R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ (inverse image of $\mathfrak q'$ under the inclusion) containing $f_1,\dots,f_c$; hence $\mathfrak q_\lambda=\mathfrak q'_\lambda/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a prime of $S_\lambda$ whose inverse image in $R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ is $\mathfrak q'_\lambda$. Claim (N) (Steps 1-3), applied to the Noetherian ring $R_\lambda$, the relative global complete intersection $S_\lambda$ (Step 4), the prime $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ and the index $i$, shows that $M_{\lambda}=R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{\mathfrak q'_\lambda}/(f_1,\dots,f_i)$ is a flat $R_\lambda$-module. For $\lambda\le\mu$ we have $\mathfrak q'_\mu\cap R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]=\mathfrak q'_\lambda$, so elements of $R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]\setminus\mathfrak q'_\lambda$ lie in $R_\mu[x_1,\dots,x_n]\setminus\mathfrak q'_\mu$ and in $P\setminus\mathfrak q'$; by the universal property of localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] the inclusions induce ring maps $R_\lambda[x]_{\mathfrak q'_\lambda}\to R_\mu[x]_{\mathfrak q'_\mu}\to P_{\mathfrak q'}$, $h/s\mapsto h/s$, which map the ideal generated by $f_1,\dots,f_i$ into the ideal generated by $f_1,\dots,f_i$. On quotients they give $R_\lambda$-linear maps $t_{\lambda\mu}:M_\lambda\to M_\mu$ and $\iota_\lambda:M_\lambda\to M_i$, all given by $h/s\mapsto h/s$ on classes; hence $t_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $t_{\mu\nu}\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=t_{\lambda\nu}$ and $\iota_\mu\circ t_{\lambda\mu}=\iota_\lambda$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), second paragraph: 'With this notation, we have (1) and (2) for each lambda'

proof.text: The system of Step 5 satisfies conditions (i) and (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-union-subrings-flat-module]. (i) An element of $M_i$ is the class of $h/s$ with $h\in P$, $s\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The finitely many coefficients of $h$ and $s$ together with generators of $R_0$ generate a subring $R_\lambda\in\Lambda$; then $h,s\in R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $s\notin\mathfrak q'_\lambda$, and the class of $h/s$ in $M_\lambda$ is mapped by $\iota_\lambda$ to the given element. (ii) Let $m\in M_\lambda$ be the class of $h/s$ ($h\in R_\lambda[x]$, $s\in R_\lambda[x]\setminus\mathfrak q'_\lambda$) with $\iota_\lambda(m)=0$, i.e. $h/s\in(f_1,\dots,f_i)P_{\mathfrak q'}$. Writing the coefficients over a common denominator, $h/s=\sum_{j\le i}(a_j/t)f_j$ in $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ with $a_j\in P$, $t\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$; by the definition of equality in a localization there is $u\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ with $u\,(th-s\sum_ja_jf_j)=0$ in $P$. Let $R_\mu\in\Lambda$ contain $R_\lambda$ and the coefficients of $u,t,a_1,\dots,a_i$ (Step 4). Then $u,t\in R_\mu[x]\setminus\mathfrak q'_\mu$, and the same equation holds in the subring $R_\mu[x]$ of $P$, so $h/s=\sum_j(a_j/t)f_j$ in $R_\mu[x]_{\mathfrak q'_\mu}$, i.e. $t_{\lambda\mu}(m)=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SV (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal, line 36767), second paragraph: 'R[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'}/(f_1,...,f_i) = colim R_lambda[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'_lambda}/(f_1,...,f_i)'

proof.text: By Steps 4-6, $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is a directed family of subrings of $R$ with union $R$, each $M_\lambda$ is a flat $R_\lambda$-module (Step 5), and $(M_i,\iota_\lambda,t_{\lambda\mu})$ satisfies the compatibilities and conditions (i), (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-union-subrings-flat-module]. That lemma gives that $M_i=P_{\mathfrak q'}/(f_1,\dots,f_i)P_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a flat $R$-module. As $i$ and $\mathfrak q$ were arbitrary, the statement follows.

split_report.summary: Followed the proof of part (2) of Stacks 00SV (algebra.tex 36783-36832). Noetherian case (Steps 1-3): R_p -> P_q' is a flat local map of Noetherian local rings (P free, Hilbert basis, 00HT); the f_j are a regular sequence in P_q'/pP_q' (fibre ring = k[x], 00SS(1) over k=kappa(p) gives fibre dimension n-c, then the regular-sequence lemma of 00SB/00SC, transported by the natural isomorphism of 0H9M); 00MG gives flatness over R_p, then over R. General case (Steps 4-7): Noetherian approximation 00SU, directed family of finite type Z-subrings, base change 00SS(1), the colimit identification written out, and 05UU(2) in the form of a directed union of subrings. New nodes: 00MG, 00SS(1), 00SU, 05UU(2) (subring form), and the natural-map form of 0H9M (the existing node lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-iso states only an abstract isomorphism). Citer lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat uses i=c; formulation matches. Statement unchanged.
